To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) innovation is a major cause for crashes, and that (2) the presence of keystone species is a major cause, and (3) the presence of innovation is a necessary condition, for recoveries.
the causes of large extinctions are (i) the extinction of a keystone species and (ii) innovation.
the causes of large extinctions are (i) innovation and (ii) the extinction of keystone species, and that the causes of recoveries are (iii) the assimilation of innovations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the causes of large and sudden changes in the structure of complex systems, in this case, biological ones.
the causes and effects of large extinctions, and with the role of innovation, and of keystone species, as proximate causes of such extinctions.
the causes of major transitions in biological evolution, and with the mechanisms by which such transitions occur.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
large extinctions and recoveries in the model are caused by the extinction of one or more keystone species or by the introduction of new interactions.
large extinctions are caused primarily by the extinction of a keystone species, but that the recovery of the system is driven by innovation.
innovation is the main cause of major and rapid changes in the structure of a coevolving system, but that keystone species are important for the size and frequency of such events.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dynamics of the system is driven by innovation and keystone extinctions.
innovation and keystone extinctions are the major causes of major crashes, and that innovation and the assimilation of keystone species are the main causes of recoveries.
innovation and keystone extinctions are the major causes of large extinctions in the model system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
major extinctions and recoveries are not random events, but can be understood and predicted from the structure of the network of interactions.
the causes of crashes and their sizes are not independent of each other.
the causes of large extinctions are not random.
